_readme: This block holds all the text of the 'Job Specific Qualifications' tab. Edit the text here; the page builds itself from it every time it loads.

JSON rules: keep the double quotes around every text value, put a comma after every item in a list except the last one, and do not add comments. Inside text, avoid double quotes (use single quotes or curly quotes instead); if you really need one, put a backslash in front of it.

Formatting inside any text value: **double asterisks** make bold, a line break is typed as a backslash followed by the letter n, and a link is written as {label|https://example.com}. Email links work too: {name|mailto:you@example.com}.

hover = the text shown in the Details box when that title or bullet is clicked. Write na (or leave the quotes empty) when there is no hover text; that item then shows the 'no extra information' message when clicked.

sectionOrder = the order of the sections on the page and in the Background list. Move a line up or down to reorder. Every id listed must exist in the sections block below; a section that is defined but not listed is simply hidden.
Section type: standard (clickable title and bullets with hover text) or links (bullets are plain links; each one needs a url instead of hover).
Avoid writing a closing script tag inside any text.

header.tagline: Technical Writer, Courseware Developer, and Trainer with 16+ years of experience writing technical courses on application development topics. Self-Learner and demystifier of all things complex.
header.status: US citizen - Holding a valid German Work Visa.

documentation.title: Documentation
documentation.intro: Spent 15 years researching, designing, authoring, and delivering technical courseware and training across a wide range of topics related to front and back end application development and deployment.

bullets.text: Authored and maintained dozens of courses on software development topics.
bullets.hover: Courses developed include: React, Node.js, Java Spring Boot, Docker, Kubernetes, and AWS services.
50% of the delivery time for each course is devoted to hands-on training based on these lab instructions.
The webinars were created and delivered for a training company in support of their marketing efforts.

bullets.text: Authored blog posts on technical topics
bullets.hover: Blogs were posted to the training company's website.
The tests evaluated students' topic knowledge before and after taking a class.

studio-recording.title: Studio & Recording
studio-recording.intro: Earlier in my career I worked as a recording engineer at recording studios in the NYC area. Recent audio engineering includes work on my own music.

bullets.text: I've been using Logic Pro for more than 10 years
bullets.hover: Recorded my album "Just Like That" entirely in Logic.

bullets.text: I'm also familiar with other DAWs including: Pro-Tools, Reaper, Ableton Live, Studio One, EnergyXT, and others.
bullets.hover: Out of the bunch, Logic is the most complete, easy to use, and musical option.

bullets.text: Recorded and mixed album of my own titled "Just Like That"
bullets.hover: The album {'Just Like That'|https://music.apple.com/us/album/just-like-that/1514534686} is available on Apple Music and other streaming services.
For my professional album credits see {Discogs.com|https://www.discogs.com/artist/832778-Mark-Pawlowski}

operating-systems.title: Operating Systems
operating-systems.hover: I am fully experienced and capable on all the major operating systems.
operating-systems.intro: I have experience working across Apple, Windows, and Linux environments.

bullets.hover: My MacBook Air M1 is the latest of many Mac computers I've owned and worked with.
I also work with this Windows 11 machine.
I work mostly with Ubuntu on virtual machines or through the WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) on Windows.

music-gear.title: Music Gear
music-gear.hover: Just for fun, here's a list of some of my music gear.
music-gear.intro: I maintain a collection of guitars, amps, modeling, recording and performing gear for my personal use as an audio engineer and singer-songwriter.

bullets.hover: This guitar plays and sounds great. I bought it at a really cool music store - {Parkway Music|https://parkwaymusic.com/} in Albany, NY.
I was planning to get a PRS SE Custom 24 but this Single Cut model felt better when I played it. It was purchased at Sam Ash in Paramus, NJ.

bullets.text: Yamaha THR10 desktop amp and modeler
bullets.hover: This tabletop amp is really easy to use and sounds amazing. I bought it used from some guy on eBay.
First heard these at a studio in NYC. I heard them before I saw them and right away I knew I had to get them.
These monitors really sound good. The ones I have are passive (the powered ones had not been released yet.)
I got this to use at some gigs I had planned. It sounds great. I could patch it right into the PA system if needed. It lets me leave the big pedalboard at home.
I got this because it sounds just like the big floorboard version, is easier to work with for recording and was dirt cheap.
It's a modeling amp that has actual knobs, wow! You can dial in great sounds without ever touching an editor program. It's also good as an FRFR amp for the Valeton gear.

This thing sounds great, is portable, is rechargeable, etc. One downside though is that it has too few physical controls - a gain control would have been nice. I tried the larger Spark amp but it sounded boxy no matter which patch it's on.
